biography: Sharing things I'm learning through my foundation work and other interests.

latestIgtvVideos.caption: Shortly after Paul Farmer’s death, I came across a series of interviews. I loved hearing him talk about why his work was so important to him. It was the next best thing to hanging out with him one last time. I hope the spirit of his work lives on for generations.
If we’re going to prevent the next pandemic, the world needs the infectious disease equivalent of firefighters. Also in this video: a cute puppy.

What if you could visit a museum exhibit about the last pandemic the world ever faced — COVID-19 — fifty years in the future? What would it reveal about how we created a world free from the threat of pandemics?
I believe that COVID-19 can be the last pandemic, and I wrote a book about how we can make that happen. You can read it on May 3.

2021 was a challenging year, but I see many reasons for optimism in 2022 including broad support for efforts to prevent the next pandemic and progress on HIV, Alzheimer’s, climate innovation, and education. You can read my full end-of-year post at the link in my bio.
I really enjoyed reading these five books this year, and I think you will too (link in bio).

Shumaila Rehmani is a polio vaccinator in Pakistan who is working to make sure every child in her community is protected from this disease.
 
While an overwhelming majority of families she visits want their children to be vaccinated, some parents, out of fear or a lack of information, refuse to have their children vaccinated.
 
But Shumaila doesn’t give up.
 
#worldpolioday

latestIgtvVideos.title: Washington State Teacher of the Year 2021
latestIgtvVideos.caption: “When we put our students' humanity first, the sky is the limit for how far our kids can go." I’m grateful to Washington State Teacher of the Year Brooke Brown for sharing with me how she helps her students learn how to love themselves and appreciate their own past.

latestIgtvVideos.title: Washington State Teacher of the Year 2021
latestIgtvVideos.caption: Brooke Brown, the 2021 Washington State Teacher of the Year, teaches ethnic studies and English to high school seniors. Her classes are a mix of history and group projects aimed at exploring identity. She was kind enough to show me one of her favorite lessons to do with her students, which was all about understanding how other people see the world.

latestIgtvVideos.title: A new way to invest in clean energy innovation
latestIgtvVideos.caption:
The world needs to eliminate greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. To make that happen, we need to invent and deploy many more clean energy products.
 
Breakthrough Energy Catalyst will jumpstart this process by bringing together partners across the public and private sectors.
 
I am optimistic that we can succeed if we act boldly together.

latestPosts.caption: The week I spend in New York for #Goalkeepers2030 and the UN General Assembly is always a highlight of my year. Last week was no exception.
At #Goalkeepers2030, I spoke with Archbishop Vicenzo Paglia about how people and relationships must remain at the center of how we use AI.

We have an opportunity—and an obligation—to ensure that AI tools are designed to improve lives and reach the people who stand to benefit most, including farmers, teachers, and health workers.  

Progress doesn’t happen on its own. It happens because the world invests in and prioritizes it. If we can combine increased generosity with the smart use of AI, there’s no limit to the progress we can make.

There are around 7,000 languages spoken worldwide, yet most AI tools are still built primarily in English. The Gates Foundation is joining a coalition of organizations to help nearly 3.4 billion people whose languages are underrepresented in AI. Over the next five years, these services will provide access to them in their own language and voice. #goalkeepers2030
I’m excited to be in New York this week to keep the conversation around AI moving forward and to build on the incredible progress we’re making. #Goalkeepers2030
Seth Rogen and Lauren Miller Rogen founded Hilarity for Charity to make sure no one has to care for a loved one with Alzheimer’s alone.

AI could be a great equalizer, but only if it’s built to benefit the people who need it most. 

That’s why the Gates Foundation is committing $1 billion over the next two years to expand access to AI and the solutions, opportunities, and knowledge that are too often inaccessible for many around the world—in health clinics, in classrooms, and on farms. 

This year’s Goalkeepers Report focuses on the urgent actions needed to ensure AI narrows the gaps between the richest and poorest rather than widening them.

AI gives us a once-in-a-generation opportunity to help more solutions reach the people who need them. But there are three things the world needs to get right first. Explore more in the 2026 Goalkeepers Report.
AI has huge potential for agriculture, especially in low-income countries—and Neema Mduma is helping lead the way with KilimoAI.
